For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo. ``` $skill-install

rising_new_repos_30d.readme_excerpt: # The Day Trader skill 11 Claude skills for day trading: scan thousands of charts, track breaking news, time every entry and exit, and replay every outcome before you risk a dollar. Free, MIT, no signup, no API key. The tools are plain Python that read free public data: Yahoo Finance charts, Nasdaq Trader's symbol lists, SEC EDGAR and the House Clerk. One scans thousands of charts for setups. Another tracks breaking news on every stock you watch. One watches a setup bar by bar and tells you the moment to get in, and another sets your stop and your target before you do. And the craziest one is the Time Machine: before you risk a dollar, it replays the rest of the session 10,000 times from the stock's own recent bars, plus every past day the same setup fired, and tells you the honest odds. And no trade goes through until you say yes. Nothing in this pack can place an order on its own. Paper trading is the default. > **Looking for the original Trader skill?** Copy an investor's 13F, the > stock screener, tax lots and rebalancing live in > [github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill). > This repo is its day-trading sequel: the Trader skill

rising_new_repos_30d.readme_excerpt: # auto-pause > [!IMPORTANT] > **This plugin was written entirely by AI.** All of its code, tests and documentation were written by Claude (Anthropic's AI) in Claude Code. I am not a programmer. What I did: > > - Came up with the idea on my own, before I knew any similar plugins existed. > - Gathered the outside research on similar plugins that shaped the design. > - Decided what the plugin should do, reviewed the work, and edited this README. Claude has two usage limits: one resets every 5 hours, the other every week. When you get close to one, this plugin makes Claude stop at a good moment and save a note (Claude calls it a "handoff") about where it left off, and give you a resume prompt to copy. After the limit resets, you paste the resume prompt into a new chat session and Claude carries on. ## How this plugin helps - You don't lose work halfway. Without it, Claude can hit the limit in the middle of a change and leave files half-edited, with no record of what it was doing. - A fresh chat uses less of your new limit. Claude's short-term memory of a chat (the "cache") runs out after an hour, so continuing the old chat after the reset makes it re-read the whole conversation at full
